name: Facebook
tip: Find the content license: it can keep applying to things you've deleted if other people shared them. Then look at where disputes go (California courts, California law).

name: TikTok
tip: TikTok can ban or suspend your account at any time, without notice. Also look for the indemnity clause, where you agree to cover TikTok's legal costs.

name: Spotify
tip: Spotify can remove content, or change or stop the service, whenever it wants. Disputes go to individual arbitration, and you give up a jury trial.

name: Netflix
tip: Most of the red flags are about disputes: binding, individual, confidential arbitration, and no class-action lawsuits.

name: Discord
tip: Discord can suspend or end your account for any reason, with or without telling you. In arbitration, the arbitrator can sanction claims it decides are frivolous.

name: X
tip: Find the $15,000 clause: break the terms and you agree to pay that much for every million posts viewed in a day. Disputes go to courts in Texas.
